boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Documented Nazareth ceremonies, recurring campus practices, and historic traditions.

cards.title: Paint the Tunnels
cards.subtitle: Student-created murals in the campus tunnel system
cards.notes: Walk the tunnel system and look closely at the student-painted walls; the university dates this continuing mural practice to the 1940s.
cards.short_summary: An enduring student art practice beneath campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Nazareth states that students have brightened its underground tunnels by painting murals since the 1940s.
cards.access_notes: Use public campus access rules and do not alter existing artwork without university authorization.

cards.title: Find Ruth, the First Tunnel Mural
cards.subtitle: Tunnel wall from Smyth Hall toward the Shults Center
cards.notes: Locate the Ruth mural while passing between Smyth Hall and the Shults Center; it anchors the later student tunnel-painting tradition.
cards.short_summary: The 1942 mural that predates the student-painted walls.
cards.evidence_claim: Nazareth identifies John C. Menihan's 1942 mural of the Biblical figure Ruth as the first tunnel mural.
cards.access_notes: View from the tunnel corridor; do not touch or add to the historic mural.

cards.title: Hear Smyth Hall Mark the Hour
cards.subtitle: Smyth Hall tower
cards.notes: Pause outside Smyth Hall around the half hour to hear the carillon, a campus sound tradition that marks time and class starts.
cards.short_summary: A 25-note campus timekeeper installed in 1975.
cards.evidence_claim: Nazareth describes the Smyth Hall carillon as a cherished tradition; it plays Westminster chimes every half hour and hour.
cards.access_notes: The university says the chimes ring 24 hours a day, seven days a week.

cards.title: Spot the Former Motherhouse Bells
cards.subtitle: Golisano Academic Center belfry
cards.notes: Look up at the Golisano Academic Center belfry and read about its three named bells, retained from the former Motherhouse.
cards.short_summary: Three historic bells connect Nazareth to the Sisters of St. Joseph.
cards.evidence_claim: Nazareth says the three Golisano Academic Center bells were rung at the former Motherhouse from 1930 until 2003.
cards.access_notes: This is a historic bell-ringing practice; the cited ringing period ended in 2003.

cards.title: Begin with First Night
cards.subtitle: New-student Convocation tradition
cards.notes: For new students, attend the candlelight ceremony after Convocation and use the reflection to connect Nazareth's founders' legacy with campus life.
cards.short_summary: A first-night reflection for incoming Golden Flyers.
cards.evidence_claim: Nazareth calls First Night a newer ceremony after new-student Convocation, where students reflect on living out the founders' legacy.
cards.access_notes: Scheduled as part of new-student orientation; consult the current orientation program for attendance details.

cards.title: Take a Finals-Season Breakfast Break
cards.subtitle: Once-a-semester Nazareth community event
cards.notes: Watch for the end-of-semester announcement and join the once-a-semester breakfast gathering, which brings students together with faculty, staff, and alumni.
cards.short_summary: A late-evening breakfast tradition more than two decades old.
cards.evidence_claim: Nazareth calls Midnight Breakfast a staple in the community for over 20 years and says it occurs once each semester.
cards.access_notes: The cited event ran 9 p.m.–midnight; verify the current semester's time and location before attending.

cards.title: Close the Year at Springfest
cards.subtitle: Campus-wide end-of-year celebration
cards.notes: Check the Campus Activities Board schedule near semester's end and take part in the all-student Springfest programming and daytime-evening activities.
cards.short_summary: Nazareth's annual end-of-year campus celebration.
cards.evidence_claim: Nazareth describes Springfest as an annual campus-wide end-of-the-year tradition hosted by the Campus Activities Board and Undergraduate Association.
cards.access_notes: Attend the all-ages activities listed in the current event schedule; do not enter any separately restricted area.

cards.title: Carry Forward the Senior Class Gift
cards.subtitle: Graduating-class philanthropy tradition
cards.notes: If participating as a graduating student, review the class-gift opportunity and direct support toward an area of campus meaningful to your class.
cards.short_summary: Graduating classes make a collective gift for future Flyers.
cards.evidence_claim: Nazareth described the Senior Class gift as a long-standing tradition in which the Class of 2014 made gifts benefiting future students.
cards.source_title: Students Learn the Impact of Philanthropy
cards.access_notes: Participation and gift options vary by graduating class; confirm current opportunities with Alumni Engagement.

cards.title: Pass a Diploma Across Generations
cards.subtitle: Nazareth Commencement legacy-family ceremony
cards.notes: Eligible Nazareth alumni can register to ceremoniously present a relative's diploma at Commencement, subject to the university's current deadline and rules.
cards.short_summary: A recent commencement tradition for Nazareth families.
cards.evidence_claim: Nazareth says its legacy-diploma tradition began in 2024, with alumni ceremoniously handing diplomas to graduating relatives.
cards.source_title: Nazareth Celebrates Commencement and Legacy Diplomas
cards.access_notes: Limited to eligible legacy family members and graduating students; current registration is required.

cards.title: Mark a Family Naz Connection
cards.subtitle: Naz Weekend ceremony for current students and Naz relatives
cards.notes: During Naz Weekend, eligible students and relatives can register for the Legacy Pinning Ceremony recognizing a continuing family connection to Nazareth.
cards.short_summary: A Naz Weekend ceremony honoring multigenerational ties.
cards.evidence_claim: Nazareth describes the Legacy Pinning Ceremony as a tradition recognizing current students and relatives who graduated from or attend Nazareth.
cards.access_notes: The cited Naz Weekend listing says registration is required; check the current schedule for eligibility and seating.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Nazareth University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-key first-weekend route through named campus landmarks, study spaces, recreation, and arts venues.

cards.title: Start at Palladoro Welcome Vista
cards.subtitle: Arrival point on the Nazareth campus map
cards.notes: Use the named welcome vista as a meeting point, then orient yourself with the campus map before choosing the next stop.
cards.short_summary: Begin with a named campus arrival landmark.
cards.evidence_claim: Nazareth’s campus map labels Palladoro Welcome Vista.
cards.access_notes: Consult the campus map for routes and visitor parking guidance.

cards.title: Locate Clock Tower Commons
cards.subtitle: Named campus landmark and computer-lab building
cards.notes: Make this your visual anchor for the weekend; it is map-listed, and some computer labs there are open around the clock.
cards.short_summary: A recognizable landmark for learning the campus layout.
cards.evidence_claim: Nazareth lists Clock Tower Commons on its campus map and says some computer labs there are open 24 hours.
cards.access_notes: Some Clock Tower Commons computer labs are open 24 hours; verify the specific lab before going.

cards.title: Settle into Wilmot Library
cards.subtitle: Campus study areas, movies, and research materials
cards.notes: Take a quiet reset in the library and identify a study area you can return to when classes begin next week.
cards.short_summary: Choose a dependable study-space stop early.
cards.evidence_claim: Nazareth identifies Wilmot Library as having study areas, movies, and research materials.
cards.access_notes: A NazCard is required for library access.

cards.title: Learn the tunnel route
cards.subtitle: Links Golisano, Shults, Smyth, the Library, and residence areas
cards.notes: Walk a short section of the mapped tunnels so you know a weather-protected route between major academic and student spaces.
cards.short_summary: Practice a practical indoor campus connection.
cards.evidence_claim: Nazareth’s Tunnel Walking Map shows tunnels connecting Golisano Academic Center, Shults, Smyth Hall, the Library, and other buildings.
cards.access_notes: Follow posted campus access rules and use the map to plan your route.

cards.title: Get your bearings at Shults Center
cards.subtitle: Student gathering place with Student Experience offices
cards.notes: Stop by the information desk, locate Student Engagement and Leadership, and note the fitness and dining services housed here.
cards.short_summary: Find key student services in one building.
cards.evidence_claim: Nazareth describes Shults Center as a student gathering place with fitness facilities and Student Experience offices.
cards.access_notes: The building lists daily hours of 7 a.m.–midnight; individual facilities may have different hours.

cards.title: Take a look at Golisano Training Center
cards.subtitle: Indoor track, courts, training facilities, and fitness center
cards.notes: Walk through the facility and note where its indoor track, courts, fitness center, and recreation opportunities are located.
cards.short_summary: Preview a campus recreation and wellness facility.
cards.evidence_claim: Nazareth says Golisano Training Center includes an indoor track, field, courts, training facilities, cafe, fitness center, and recreation opportunities.
cards.access_notes: Fitness facilities are available to students with a NazCard; check facility-specific hours.

cards.title: Walk the outdoor track
cards.subtitle: Golden Flyer Stadium athletic area
cards.notes: If you are part of the Naz community, use the outdoor track for a daylight walk and get familiar with the stadium side of campus.
cards.short_summary: A simple outdoor movement stop on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Nazareth states that the outdoor track is open to the Naz community and publishes stadium hours for athletes.
cards.access_notes: The outdoor track is open to the Naz community; stadium athlete hours are Mon–Thu 8 a.m.–10 p.m., Fri 8 a.m.–8 p.m., and weekends noon–4 p.m.

cards.title: See what is showing at Arts Center Gallery
cards.subtitle: Nazareth Arts Center
cards.notes: Check the current exhibition and spend time with a few works; use the gallery’s posted schedule before making the walk over.
cards.short_summary: Make room for a campus visual-arts visit.
cards.evidence_claim: Nazareth’s Arts Center Gallery presents diverse artwork and lists Friday and Saturday hours of noon–8 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Posted regular hours are Sun noon–5 p.m., Tue–Thu noon–5 p.m., and Fri–Sat noon–8 p.m.; specific shows may differ.

cards.title: Continue upstairs to Colacino Gallery
cards.subtitle: Second floor of the Arts Center, Art and Design wing
cards.notes: Pair this with the Arts Center Gallery visit and look for the current exhibition in the second-floor Art and Design wing.
cards.short_summary: A second, clearly located campus gallery stop.
cards.evidence_claim: Nazareth says the Margaret Colacino Gallery is on the Arts Center’s second floor and serves students and the greater Rochester community.
cards.access_notes: Posted regular hours are Wednesday–Sunday, noon–5 p.m.; confirm exhibition-specific hours first.

cards.title: End at Glazer Music Performance Center
cards.subtitle: 550-seat performance hall and education center
cards.notes: Find the performance center while daylight remains, then check the Arts Center calendar for a future public performance that fits your schedule.
cards.short_summary: Finish by locating a major campus performance venue.
cards.evidence_claim: Nazareth identifies Glazer Music Performance Center as a 550-seat performance hall and education center that opened in 2018.
cards.access_notes: Performance availability and ticketing vary by event; consult the Arts Center calendar before attending.
